summary: New Hampshire has no sales tax, but an alcoholic drink served at a restaurant or bar is a taxable meal under its Meals and Rooms Tax (RSA 78-A), at 8.5%, which this rate is.

citations.title: NH DRA: Meals & Rooms (Rentals) Tax
citations.quote: The tax rate is 8.5% for taxable periods beginning October 1, 2021.

citations.title: RSA 78-A:3 VIII, Meals and Rooms Tax definitions
citations.quote: Beverage includes an alcoholic beverage provided with or without food.

citations.title: RSA 78-A:6 II(g), Meals and Rooms Tax
citations.quote: Eight and a half percent of the charge for taxable meals over $1.00, provided that fractions of cents shall be rounded up to the next whole cent.

notes: As the NH food.prepared rule: the Meals and Rooms Tax is a separate state tax, not in OpenTaxRate's general rates (which are 0 in NH); this rule's rate is that tax. RSA 78-A:3 VIII counts an alcoholic beverage, with or without food, as a beverage in a taxable meal. Before 2021-10-01 the rate was 9%: not researched.

summary: New Hampshire has no general sales or use tax on ordinary tangible-goods rentals.

citations.title: New Hampshire RSA 78-D:1 II, Findings and Purpose (effective July 9, 2009)
citations.quote: The state of New Hampshire does not impose a sales tax on customers making purchases of goods and services in New Hampshire, nor on goods and services purchased by its residents out of state for use, storage, or consumption in New Hampshire.

notes: Date is the statute’s printed effective date, used as earliest verified; this is a finding of an already existing absence of sales tax. General sales tax only; special taxes outside these codes not modeled. No general local sales taxes under existing NH convention.
